name: Multi-Scale Pure-Vision Prototype and Boosted-Tree Stacking Ensemble
summary: Each patient's slides are represented across Virchow2, UNI2-h, and H-Optimus-1 as discrete tile-prototype proportions and PCA patient-mean vectors. Inside each training fold, a balanced logistic meta-learner stacks out-of-fold probabilities from multi-scale prototype classifiers and boosted trees using H&E features alone. Repeated nested patient and site-grouped cross-validation benchmarks this stack against chance baselines and the simple logistic reference. Bootstrap intervals establish whether H&E subtype predictability is broad, partial, site-confounded, or insufficient.
preprocessing: Pool all diagnostic slides of each patient into one patient-level tile bag (up to 128 tiles per slide) and enforce strict patient-ID split grouping across all 802 labelled patients while excluding the 259 unlabelled patients from supervised fitting and scoring.
Exclude all forbidden clinical, immunohistochemistry receptor (er, pr, her2), histological_type, age, stage, RNA, and site variables from model inputs and preprocessing.

Inside each training fold only, apply per-tile L2 unit-norm scaling followed by training-fold standardisation and PCA reduction (128 dimensions per pure-vision encoder at tile level; 64 dimensions across concatenated pure-vision patient-mean vectors).

Fit K-means morphological centroids strictly on training-fold tiles (drawing up to 96 tiles per patient during centroid fitting so multi-slide patients do not dominate cluster geometry), then map all tiles of each patient to L1-normalised prototype share histograms with 1e-4 additive smoothing.
Compute inverse-prevalence class weights strictly from training-fold PAM50 counts and pass them to every base classifier and the logistic meta-learner.

training.convergence_check: Record K-means inertia convergence (tol 1e-4), per-iteration training and validation weighted multi-class log-loss curves for all boosting members verifying trailing-stage slope stabilisation, and L-BFGS gradient convergence (tol 1e-4) for base and meta logistic models.

metrics: Out-of-fold four-class macro-F1 with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference versus majority-class null and stratified class-prior null baselines with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs
Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference versus simple patient-mean regularised logistic regression reference with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Proportion of class-prior multi-class log-loss (Shannon entropy) explained out-of-fold with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Macro and per-class one-vs-rest AUROC (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs
Per-class precision, recall, and F1 across LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 (highlighting Her2 recall and LumA-versus-LumB confusion)
Site-held-out grouped CV (19 collection sites) macro-F1 and paired gain over chance baselines with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Fold-wise boosting deviance curves, K-means inertia stabilisation, and logistic solver convergence rates
allowed_conclusions: Selects exactly one objective conclusion from 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs on identical 802-patient splits: Broad predictability (macro-F1 beats chance in both patient and 19-site CV and all four classes beat chance), Partial predictability (overall macro-F1 beats chance in both CVs but at least one class 95% CI includes or falls below chance), Site-confounded predictability (patient CV beats chance but site-held-out paired 95% CI includes or falls below zero), or Insufficient evidence (patient CV paired 95% CI over chance includes or falls below zero), plus whether multi-scale prototype-and-tree stacking improves over the simple linear reference; strictly scoped to standalone TCGA-BRCA H&E features without claiming incremental clinical utility or biological mechanism.
rationale: Quantising variable-length tile bags (D6) into compact prototype proportions curbs high-dimensional overfitting (D3) and dampens continuous site stain shifts (D4) while preserving focal phenotypes lost in patient averages. Balanced boosted trees and meta-stacking capture non-linear interactions for minority Her2 and LumA/LumB separation (D1).
